## Indeterminable Values by Variable and Sample Type
```{r proc1}

# select relevant variables from data frame sample_categories
samples <- sample_categories %>% 
  select(article_id, category, info)

# join procedures_data with samples 
procedures_by_category <- procedures_data %>% 
  left_join(samples, by = "article_id") %>%
  mutate(clinical = category == 1) 

# count the tasks with clinical and non-clinical samples
row_counts <- procedures_by_category %>%
  count(clinical)

# select variables of interest
# create a boolean variable for clinical vs. non-clinical studies
# count the number of indeterminables for each variable
indeterminables_by_cat <- procedures_by_category %>%
  select(7:29, clinical) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 1:23, 
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>% 
  filter(value == "indeterminable") %>%
  count(clinical, variable) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = clinical, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(`count_clinical` = `TRUE`, `count_non_clinical` = `FALSE`) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_clinical = (count_clinical / 53 * 100),
    pct_non_clinical = (count_non_clinical / 53 * 100)
  ) %>%
  select(variable, count_clinical, pct_clinical, count_non_clinical, pct_non_clinical)

# calculate the totals across all variables
total_ind <- indeterminables_by_cat %>%
  summarise(
    variable = "total",
    count_clinical = sum(count_clinical),
    pct_clinical = (sum(count_clinical) / (53 * 23)) * 100, 
    count_non_clinical = sum(count_non_clinical),
    pct_non_clinical = (sum(count_non_clinical) / (53 * 23)) * 100
  )

# bind the total row to the main table
indeterminables_by_cat <- bind_rows(indeterminables_by_cat, total_ind)

indeterminables_by_cat |>
  kable() |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

```

### Plot 1
```{r proc2}

# Filter out the "total" row for better visualization
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_by_cat %>%
  filter(variable != "total") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
    names_to = "sample_type", 
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_type = recode(sample_type,
                         "pct_clinical" = "Clinical",
                         "pct_non_clinical" = "Non-Clinical")
  )

# sort percentages of interderminables in descending order
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_dot_data %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(max_percentage = max(percentage, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, max_percentage, .desc = FALSE))

# Create the dot plot
plot1 <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data, 
                aes(x = percentage, y = variable, color = sample_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sample Type",
    values = c("Clinical" = "#31688E", "Non-Clinical" = "#35B779")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Indeterminable Values by Variable and Sample Type",
    x = "Percentage of Indeterminable Values",
    y = "Variable"
  )  +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1))  # Show x-axis as percentages

print(plot1)

```

### Plot 2
```{r proc3}

# Prepare the data for plotting
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_by_cat %>%
  filter(variable != "total") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
    names_to = "sample_type", 
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_type = recode(sample_type,
                         "pct_clinical" = "Clinical",
                         "pct_non_clinical" = "Non-Clinical")
  )

# Create the dot plot
plot2 <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data, 
                aes(x = sample_type, y = percentage, color = variable)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Variable") +
  labs(
    title = "Indeterminable Values by Variable and Sample Type",
    x = "Sample Type",
    y = "Percentage of Indeterminable Values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1))  # Show y-axis as percentages

print(plot2)

```
